issue.title: test_completion_extras relative-age tests fail on any host whose timezone differs from the configured SASE timezone: _stamp uses host-local time, relative_age uses configured-tz local_now
issue.description:
Both tests fail deterministically on a clean tree at master, with no local changes, on any host whose system timezone is not the configured SASE timezone (US Eastern on the maintainer's setup). Observed on a UTC host (`date +%Z` prints UTC, `TZ` unset): they failed on a clean `git stash -u` tree and again with an unrelated diff applied, every run.

Root cause: the test helper `_stamp` in `tests/ace/tui/command_line/test_completion_extras.py` builds history stamps from `datetime.now().astimezone()`, i.e. the HOST-local wall clock. `relative_age` in `src/sase/ace/tui/command_line/extras.py` parses the stamp as a naive time and attaches the tzinfo of `_local_now()`, which is `sase.core.time.local_now()`, the CONFIGURED timezone. With a UTC host and an Eastern config, every stamp lands 4-5 hours in the future, `elapsed < 0` is true, and `relative_age` returns "just now" instead of `30s ago` / `2h ago`:

    AssertionError: assert False  where 'just now' = relative_age('260925_172150')   (test_relative_age_buckets)
    AssertionError: assert 'just now  ✓' == '2h ago  ✓'                                (test_recent_rows_carry_age_and_exit_mark)

Not intermittent: the failure depends only on the host/configured timezone offset, not on timing or load. Fix: build `_stamp` from `sase.core.time.local_now()` (the same reference `relative_age` uses), or pass an explicit `now=` into `relative_age` in the tests. Introduced with the dynamic completion sources commit (fad9b5d03) that added the test file.

payload.description: Sibling timezone-mismatch defect (configured-tz vs host/naive datetimes); fixes touch similar datetime conventions

payload.entry: Fixed in the sase-17x.13.10 landing. The _stamp helper in tests/ace/tui/command_line/test_completion_extras.py now stamps with datetime.now(get_timezone()), the same configured-zone reference relative_age's _local_now uses, instead of host-local datetime.now().astimezone(). Verified: the file fails 2/21 under TZ=UTC before the change and passes 21/21 under TZ=UTC and TZ=America/Los_Angeles after. The command_line_empty_state visual test had the same host-vs-configured-zone stamp bug and was fixed the same way.
